name: Valero

profile.reading:
This facility, recorded as Valero Wiserman, is attributed to Valero Energy Corporation and located within Bexar County, Texas, the county that contains San Antonio, where Valero has its corporate headquarters. Valero is one of the largest independent petroleum refining and marketing companies in the world, a Fortune 500 company operating refineries, ethanol plants, and a nationwide fuel distribution and retail network across North America. A company of that scale and complexity requires substantial internal information technology infrastructure to support refinery process control and historian systems, logistics and pipeline scheduling, commodities trading, financial reporting, and corporate administration, and it would be unusual for a company of Valero's size not to operate dedicated data processing facilities near its headquarters campus.

The Center for Land Use Interpretation, which documents significant industrial and corporate land uses across the country, has separately described Valero's San Antonio headquarters campus as a substantial corporate real estate presence in the city, consistent with a company that also maintains supporting technical facilities nearby. Beyond that general corporate context, however, this entry could not confirm a specific street address, construction date, square footage, or power capacity for the Valero Wiserman building itself. The geographic coordinates associated with this record, when checked, map to an area of San Antonio's Westover Hills technology corridor that other public mapping data associates with an unrelated data center campus operated by a different company entirely, rather than with a confirmed Valero-branded building, so the precise location of this facility should be treated as unresolved rather than confirmed.

Valero does not publish a public directory of its internal data center locations, which is typical for a company whose core business is industrial rather than information technology itself. Enterprise data centers supporting refining, trading, and logistics operations are rarely marketed the way commercial colocation facilities are, since their purpose is internal operational support rather than attracting outside tenants. The lack of published detail here reflects that difference in business model rather than any unusual secrecy, and this entry should be read as identifying a facility associated with Valero's Bexar County corporate presence, with its precise site characteristics currently undocumented in public sources.

reading:
Valero Energy Corporation is one of the largest independent petroleum refiners in the world, a Fortune 500 company headquartered at One Valero Way on the north side of San Antonio. It is in this registry as an enterprise, meaning it runs a data centre for itself rather than selling capacity to anyone. Refining is a data heavy business in ways that are not obvious from outside, covering crude and product trading, refinery scheduling and optimisation, pipeline and terminal logistics, wholesale and retail fuel supply, and the corporate systems of a company running more than a dozen refineries, and that work has historically sat on infrastructure the company owns.

The single row is mapped as an industrial building named Valero Wiserman, tagged with Valero as operator and with a telecom data centre tag, first drawn in 2017 and carrying no address at all. Its coordinates place it on Wiseman Boulevard in the Westover Hills district of west San Antonio, in Bexar County, postcode 78251, which makes the stored name almost certainly a misspelling of the street. That is roughly nine miles from the One Valero Way headquarters campus, so this is a separate site and not the head office machine room. The immediate surroundings explain the location. Within a few hundred metres sit two CPS Energy substations, the VLSI substation and the Verde Circle substation, the TowerJazz semiconductor fab on Westover Hills Boulevard, a Capital Group campus on Wiseman Boulevard, and the industrial parcel mapped as Microsoft's SAT14 site. Westover Hills is San Antonio's oldest data centre corridor, and local reporting has named Valero among the companies that built there for their own use rather than to lease.

Two other Valero facts are established and neither belongs to this row. A Texas accessibility filing records a project titled Valero HQ Stabilization and Data Center Construction at One Valero Way, a 25,416 square foot second floor remodel of Building A costing about 600,000 dollars and running from August 2019 to May 2020, which is data centre work at the headquarters rather than at Wiseman Boulevard. Separately, Valero's credit card operations centre at 7201 Canyon Drive in Amarillo is a 34,585 square foot office with an on site data centre, built in 2003 on 4.19 acres and offered for sale as a net leased investment with Valero's lease running to March 2028. That building is not in this registry at all, so the facility count here understates Valero's own data centre footprint while the one row it does hold carries no measurements.

No megawatt figure, floor area or construction date for the Wiseman Boulevard building was found in any public source, and none should be assumed. The corridor's history shows why guessing is dangerous. In July 2011 Stream Data Centers sold a 150,000 square foot Westover Hills shell on 33 acres, served by two 30 MW utility feeds from a pair of 300 MW substations, to a Fortune 100 buyer it never named. Those substation and feed ratings are utility capacity, not anything a tenant could draw, and the buyer has never been publicly identified.
